body:
## Summary

Fixes #2498.

In link-foundation/package-registry-manager#27, a work session was reported on the pull request as **"⚠️ Container OOM event during a failed work session"**. Telegram's diagnostics called the OOM event the **Cause**. Neither report gave the real reason the session stopped.

What actually happened (full timeline in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2498/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/README.md)):

- 19:32 / 19:38: a `rustc` child was OOM-killed during parallel `cargo` builds. The OOM event was real, but the session kept working.
- 19:40:42: Claude stopped with `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`.
- 19:41:03: solve exited **1** with `❌ ⚠️ SUBSCRIPTION/ACCESS UNAVAILABLE — CLAUDE stopped: Authentication expired …`.
- Docker's `State.OOMKilled` is sticky and container-wide (moby/moby#43564), so it was still `true` when the container exited.

## Root causes

1. **The PR notice ignored the detected deliberate stop.** `buildKillCompletionSections()` already found the `subscription-blocked` marker (#2408), but `announceKillOnPullRequest()` → `buildKillRecoveryNotice()` was never given it.
2. **The diagnostics kept the label "Cause: container OOM event"**, even after the deliberate stop had been reported.
3. **Upstream (start-command 0.35.1)**: `$ --status` derives `memoryExhausted: true` and `exitReason: memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)` from the sticky flag alone, for any exit code. hive-mind then showed that as a second, independent piece of evidence. Filed as **link-foundation/start#180**, with a reproduction (`experiments/issue-2498-start-command-exit-reason.cjs`), a workaround and a suggested fix.

## Changes

- `src/session-kill-recovery.lib.mjs`: `buildKillRecoveryNotice()` accepts `deliberateStop`. With an earlier OOM event the notice becomes:
  - title: "ℹ️ Work session stopped on its own — the earlier container OOM event did not cause it";
  - it leads with **Why the work session stopped**, quoting the stop line from the log;
  - the OOM event follows as "Earlier event (not the cause of this stop)", with "OOM event observed at" and "OOM event diagnostics".

  A deliberate stop followed by a real kill gets "Working session was killed after solve had already stopped on its own".
- `src/session-monitor.kill-sections.lib.mjs` and `src/session-monitor.lib.mjs`: forward `deliberateStop` to the PR notice. The Telegram diagnostics use the "not the cause" variant.
- `src/session-kill-diagnostics.lib.mjs`:
  - `formatKillDiagnosticsSection(…, { notTheCause })` uses the label "Event" and the title "Container OOM event diagnostics (not the cause of this stop)".
  - `describeKillCause()` folds the flag-derived upstream memory-exhaustion report into `oomKilled` instead of listing it as separate evidence. Real upstream detections, such as log markers, are still passed through.
- `src/locales/{en,ru,hi,zh}.lino`: new `event` / `event_diagnostics` strings.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-2498/`: the three PR comments, the gist (identical to the intermediate log apart from shortened SHAs), solve's failure log, and the case study.
- `.changeset/oom-false-positive-2498.md`: one patch changeset covering the fix and the follow-up below.

### Follow-up to the review on this PR

The [review comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2499) raised three points (1–3); item 4 is the debug output added to settle the first one. Details are in the case study, section "Follow-up: owner feedback on PR #2499".

1. **"One OOM event may have killed multiple tasks at once"** ([meta-language#196](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5985077141)). That session ran on the same host at the same time. Its log ([excerpt](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/meta-language-196-log-excerpt.txt)) shows five `formal-ai-corpus-memory` runs `Killed` (exit 137) one after another, at 19:37:53 and 19:44:03.
   - Each container lost several processes. The kills came one by one at the container's own 2.9 GB limit: 25% of the 11.7 GB host, under `ulimit -v` caps of 8 GB and 4 GB. Host memory stayed at 4.6 GB available or more, so this was not one host-wide event.
   - What ended **both** sessions within 3½ minutes was the same thing: the shared Claude OAuth token could not be refreshed (19:40:42 and 19:44:03).
   - So the OOM detection and the no-recovery decision worked as expected; the *report* was wrong in both sessions. The fix above corrects it for both.
   - The kill notice said "10.4 GB of 11.7 GB RAM available". That is host RAM, which the meta-language audit read as an "11.7 GB limit". So the logs now carry the container's own limit and OOM counters (item 4 below).
2. **Random 30–90 s delay before recovery.** Every automatic recovery now waits its own random delay before it starts:
   - `src/session-kill-policy.lib.mjs`: `resolveSessionKillResumeDelayRange()` / `pickSessionKillResumeDelayMs()`; new option `--session-kill-resume-delay <min-max>` (default `30-90`, `0` disables) or `HIVE_MIND_SESSION_KILL_RESUME_DELAY`; documented in `docs/CONFIGURATION*.md`.
   - `src/session-kill-resume.lib.mjs`: monitor-driven recoveries, both in place and in a fresh session, sleep before the launch. Each session is handled under its own in-flight guard, so one session's wait does not block the others.
   - `src/solve.tool-kill-resume.lib.mjs`: solve's in-process resume after a tool OOM kill logs `⏳ Waiting Ns before resuming …` and sleeps.
3. **Latest dependencies and start-command features.**
   - `npm outdated` for the direct dependencies is empty: all are at their latest versions.
   - `start-command@0.35.1` and `@link-assistant/agent@0.26.11` are the latest releases.
   - start provides everything hive-mind uses. The remaining gaps are reported upstream: link-foundation/start#180 (flag-derived `memoryExhausted`), **link-foundation/start#181** (no random delay for `--on-kill-resume`), **link-foundation/start#182** (no cgroup `oom`/`oom_kill`/peak in `--status`).
4. **Debug output** (`src/solve.resource-diagnostics.lib.mjs`, `src/session-kill-diagnostics.lib.mjs`):
   - every resource snapshot now reads the task's cgroup (`memory.max/current/peak`, `memory.events` `oom` and `oom_kill`; cgroup v2 with a v1 fallback);
   - it logs `Container memory (cgroup v2): … used of 2.9 GB limit, peak …; processes killed by the OOM killer so far: N`;
   - the `📈 [RESOURCES]` marker stores these values;
   - the kill diagnosis quotes them. `oom_kill > oom` points to a host-wide OOM, and `oom_kill > 1` shows that several processes were killed.

## How to reproduce / tests

`tests/issue-2498-oom-false-positive.test.mjs` replays the incident:

- fixture: the real log tail in `tests/fixtures/issue-2498/session-log-tail.txt`;
- input: the exact `$ --status` record (`exitCode 1`, `oomKilled true`, `memoryExhausted true`, `memoryExhaustedReason 'Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true'`, `exitReason 'memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)'`);
- coverage: `describeKillCause`, the Telegram sections, the PR notice, `announceKillOnPullRequest` and a full `monitorSessions` pass.

Against the code before this PR, **5 of 6 tests fail**. With the fix, all 6 pass. The existing #2134, #2301 and #2408 kill/OOM suites still pass.

Follow-up tests:

- `tests/issue-2498-recovery-delay.test.mjs` (6 tests): the default range, the flag and environment settings, sleep before launch, three sessions killed together getting different delays, no wait for a refused recovery, and the in-process resume.
- `tests/issue-2498-cgroup-memory-diagnostics.test.mjs` (6 tests): cgroup v2, v2 with `max`, v1, no cgroup, marker round-trip including old markers, the log warning, and the kill-diagnosis evidence.
- The kill/OOM tests that run real recoveries set `HIVE_MIND_SESSION_KILL_RESUME_DELAY=0`, so they do not wait.

```
node --test tests/issue-2498-*.test.mjs
```

Upstream reproduction:

```
npm pack start-command@0.35.1 && tar xzf start-command-0.35.1.tgz
node experiments/issue-2498-start-command-exit-reason.cjs ./package
# exit=1 oomKilled=true -> exitReason="memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)" memory={"memoryExhausted":true,...}
```

## Remaining uncertainty

- The logs cannot prove or rule out that memory pressure contributed to the OAuth refresh failure. Nothing in them links the two.
- Naming the OOM victim (e.g. "rustc was OOM-killed at 19:38") is listed as a possible follow-up in the case study.
- Resource snapshots are taken at phase boundaries, not continuously, so a brief host-wide OOM in the 19:32–19:44 window cannot be fully excluded. The new cgroup counters (`oom` vs `oom_kill`) will answer this for future incidents.

title: fix(session-monitor): don't present an earlier OOM event as the cause of a deliberate stop; stagger OOM recoveries (#2498)
